philosophy: A raster icon is not a partition of the plane — it is a PAINTING: an ordered stack of complete, simple, idealized shapes, each drawn whole and then partially hidden by what was painted after it. vectorizer.ai's real edge (confirmed by our IKEA forensics: hidden-layer completion, letters redrawn on top) is that it inverts the painter, not the partition. Every visible boundary belongs to exactly ONE shape — the one on top — so seams are not something you fix, they are something the representation cannot express. Symmetry, templates, and fairness become per-shape global properties of COMPLETE outlines, not of visible fragments. Vectorization = inverse rendering under a minimum-description-length prior, verified by deterministic re-rasterization.
method_name: INVERSE PAINTER — Layered Amodal Scene Vectorization (shape-stack inference with owned-boundary fitting)
core_idea: Replace the flat region tiling with a scene S = (background, s_1..s_K): complete closed shapes with colors and a z-order, chosen so that painter's-algorithm rasterization of S reproduces the label map. Each crack-graph interface between two regions is assigned a single OWNER (the occluding shape); the occluded shape has no boundary there at all — it is amodally completed underneath using its own prior (template, continuation, symmetry). Fitting data terms apply only to owned arcs; amodal segments carry pure fairness energy and can never spawn corners or wobble. Because a boundary is one curve belonging to one shape, hairline gaps/overlaps between independently fit neighbors are structurally impossible, and because shapes are complete, every regularizer (circle, mirror, rotation, template) operates on the whole object even when 60% of it is hidden. The whole thing stays deterministic: every hypothesis is accepted or rejected by re-rasterizing the stack and comparing to the labels.
pipeline:
STAGE 0 — Segmentation (unchanged, reuse): compact_palette + Lab labeling + ICM Potts + sliver merge + enclosed-counter rescue -> label map L, palette anchors. Alpha fix folded in here: composite source over nothing (premultiplied), treat fully-transparent as a first-class 'void' label so background becomes an inferable bottom shape rather than hardcoded white.

STAGE 1 — Boundary/junction graph: build_region_graph (Kopf–Lischinski crack graph) gives regions, junction nodes (degree>=3 crack vertices), and interface arcs A_ij (maximal crack chains between junctions, shared by regions i,j). Subpixel-refine arc geometry once, at native density (existing midpoint sampling). This graph is the single source of boundary truth for the rest of the pipeline.

STAGE 2 — Z-order inference (the 'above' graph): for each ordered region pair (i,j) accumulate votes v(i>j) that i occludes j:
  (a) T-junction continuation cue: at junction J where arcs a1=A_kj and a2=A_ki meet arc a3=A_ij, if a1 continues a2 through J — tangent gap dTheta<=25 deg and optional curvature agreement — then j's/i's far boundary is the 'hat' of a T and the shape behind is cut: vote w = exp(-(dTheta/20deg)^2) * min(len(a1),len(a2),cap=30px) for the hat-owner being ON TOP. This is the classic amodal rule: the stem belongs to the occluded shape.
  (b) Completion-simplicity cue: tentatively complete region j across A_ij by smooth continuation; if completed-j has lower description length (fewer inflections/primitives, existing _segment_cost) than fragment-j, vote i>j with weight proportional to the DL drop.
  (c) Enclosure: region fully inside another's filled outline -> inside is above (weight 2.0), except MDL prefers a true hole (letter counters: keep hole if 'background-colored disk on top' costs more).
  (d) Priors: smaller area above larger (0.3*log area ratio); glyph-like components strongly above; the border-touching max-area region is forced bottom.
Resolve to a global order by weighted feedback-arc-set heuristic: initial order by net vote sum, then iterated adjacent-swap until no swap reduces violated vote weight (K<=~100 shapes, trivial cost). Cyclic clusters (interlocking rings) are detected as unresolved strongly-connected components -> handled in Stage 5's fallback ladder (split one shape at the crossing into two stacked lobes, or region-native fit for just that cluster).
Abutting flat-design pairs (no junction evidence either way): declare owner = the shape whose completion is simpler; the other is still extended underneath, so the emission is identical to a real occlusion — 'abut' is just occlusion with zero hidden area plus a 0.75px safety apron.

STAGE 3 — Amodal completion: candidate complete shapes per region, bottom-up in z:
  For region r, owned(r) = arcs where r is the owner; gaps = arc intervals covered by shapes above. Candidates, in MDL order:
  (a) TEMPLATES: circle, ellipse (Fitzgibbon direct fit), rectangle/rounded-rect (PCA axes + robust extent + corner-radius from owned corner arcs), capsule, regular N-gon, star — least-squares on owned crack points ONLY. Accept iff owned-point RMS <= 0.6px, max <= 1.25px, AND the completed template's hidden area is covered exclusively by shapes above r in z (containment test against L + order). Generalizes complete_occluded_rectangles/_complete_occlusions from a hack into the core.
  (b) MERGED-REGION HYPOTHESES: same-color regions r1,r2 whose boundary arcs were linked by continuation votes across an occluder c propose ONE shape covering r1 u r2 u (strip under c). Gap bridged by template refit over both fragments' owned points, or by a single clothoid/biarc matching endpoint positions+tangents of the owned arcs (existing _clothoid_fit with Procrustes, _fit_biarc). Cap: <=2 bridges per shape initially. This is how the IKEA oval and a bar-crossed circle come back whole.
  (c) FREE-FORM: owned arcs joined by amodal bridge curves = one closed loop. Bridges are pure-fairness Euler-spiral/biarc segments (minimize curvature variation, G1 to owned tangents; G2 when both owned ends have stable curvature estimates). The loop then goes to Stage 4 fitting with per-sample weights: owned samples get the full directional-interval data term, bridge samples get weight 0 (fairness only). Bridges must stay strictly inside (region above)'s area, dilated -0.25px — verifier enforces.
  (d) GLYPHS: components flagged glyph-like (existing baseline/cap-height machinery + stroke-width statistics) become top-layer shapes fitted with the text-safe profile (exists, currently off), and optionally snapped to a font_match outline via Procrustes IF the coverage residual beats the free-form fit — a deterministic template prior, not generation.

STAGE 4 — Per-shape fitting and idealization: each shape's complete loop is fit ONCE with fit_loop_paper / fit_segment_midpoints, data term restricted to owned samples (weight vector threaded through the DP's interval constraint: amodal nodes get infinite interval). Corner CNN runs only on owned arcs; a lower shape passing under an occluder is G1/G2-continuous through the junction BY CONSTRUCTION — junction corners exist only on the occluder's outline, whose vertex is pinned to the crack-graph junction node (cross-region consensus becomes trivial: one shape, one vertex). Then the FULL Sec-6 regularizer family runs per complete shape and across shapes: circle snap, mirror at ARBITRARY axis (test principal axes + dominant edge directions of the complete outline — cheap now that the shape is whole), rotation about shape centroid, repeated-shape unification by complete-outline Procrustes (no longer needs identical primitive decomposition — compare sampled outlines, then re-emit one canonical shape K times). Accuracy budget: 1–2px Hausdorff measured on OWNED arcs only; amodal parts unconstrained except by Stage-5 consistency. Snapshot+revert as today.

STAGE 5 — Stack selection + verification (MDL, greedy with ladder): choose per-shape candidate minimizing E = sum_s lambda_c * DL(s) + lambda_d * Raster mismatch + lambda_K * K, subject to the HARD verifier: rasterize the stack back-to-front at 4x (render_regions) and require per-visible-region IoU >= 0.98 relative to L's regions, no disagreement blob > 3px diameter, owned-arc bidirectional Hausdorff within the existing backstop. Greedy: shapes bottom-up, cheapest candidate that verifies wins; on failure demote to next candidate (template -> merged -> free-form -> region-native fit of just that region, still inserted as a stack layer so its neighbors KEEP their owned boundaries). Fallback is per-shape and local — the image never globally degrades.

STAGE 6 — Color and emission: per-shape fill re-estimated as robust Lab mean of source pixels in (visible region eroded 1px) — fixes anchors-as-final-colors. SVG emitted back-to-front in z-order; every occluded shape's outline extends >=0.75px past the interface under its occluder (apron), so no renderer rounding can ever open a gap; background is a full-canvas bottom shape (color-estimated or transparent). Gradient-stack shapes and stroked centerlines slot in as shape kinds (a stroke is a shape whose outline is generated from its centerline — reuse _detect_stroke).

Thresholds philosophy: all acceptance decisions are (soft MDL score) + (hard deterministic verifier); thresholds bias PERMISSIVE on hypothesis generation and STRICT on verification, so tuning risk concentrates in the one place a wrong answer is caught by re-rasterization.
small_images: Tiny loops (<=18px^2, and generally <=32px icons) stop being fit as curves at all: they get template-first COVERAGE MATCHING against the anti-aliased source. For each template (square, diamond, circle, rounded-square, capsule, N-gon) with 3-6 parameters, minimize sum over pixels of |analytic pixel coverage(template) - observed alpha/soft label|; 20-50 anti-aliased pixels over-determine 5 parameters, so subpixel-exact size/position/rotation is recoverable where curve fitting is hopeless. The 4x MiniNet SR raster is used only as initialization; the residual is computed against the NATIVE raster (consistent with the bitmap-native memory note). Occlusion completion compounds the win: a tiny circle pinched by a neighboring shape is completed to a full circle from its owned arc instead of yielding a crescent of pixel stairs. The tiny-safe corner policy turns ON for owned arcs of small shapes, and the per-shape fallback ladder means a failed tiny fit costs one shape, not the icon. Gate: dedicated 16px/24px icon suite scored on roundness/squareness/centering, human-checked.
text: Letters are top-layer shapes — the VAI forensic secret becomes native representation. Glyph-like components (stroke-width statistics + baseline/cap-height clustering, both already implemented) route to the glyph layer: (1) they always own 100% of their outline (they occlude everything, so underlying shapes complete smoothly beneath them — no more letter-shaped bites with independently fit rims); (2) the text-safe fitting profile is ON for this layer, and the destructive whole-image IoU gate is replaced by a glyph-scale coverage-matching gate, so a valid 5-8 primitive glyph is never replaced by 29-86 staircase lines; (3) the tiny-safe corner policy and a halved collapse window (8*spacing) apply on glyph loops so adjacent true letter corners survive — recall loss localized to the one layer where it matters; (4) baseline/cap-height/x-height alignment and per-letter repeated-shape unification (two 'o's -> one outline reused) run within the layer; (5) font_match is promoted from preview to a deterministic template PRIOR: if the conservative gate fires, the matched font outline is Procrustes-fit per glyph and accepted only if its coverage residual beats the free-form fit — verifiable, zero hallucination risk. 150k-wordmark corpus drives the gate calibration.
symmetry_idealization: Idealization becomes per-shape and global because shapes are COMPLETE: a circle that is 60% hidden is still fit as a full circle from its owned arc (template acceptance needs only RMS<=0.6px on owned points); a shield occluded at the bottom still gets mirror symmetry over its whole outline. Completeness makes previously unaffordable regularizers cheap: mirror axes at ANY angle (candidates = principal axes + dominant edge directions of the complete outline, scored by complete-outline chamfer self-distance under reflection), rotation about the true shape centroid, and repeat unification by outline Procrustes instead of identical primitive decomposition. Bounding: the accuracy budget (1-2px) is enforced ONLY on owned arcs — visible evidence is sacred, hidden geometry is free — and every idealization must survive the stack re-rasterization verifier (visible-region IoU >= 0.98, no >3px disagreement blob), with snapshot+revert exactly as today. So regularity can never repaint what the user sees; it can only clean up what perception already assumes.
artifact_elimination: SEAMS: structurally impossible — an interface is one crack chain owned by exactly one shape; the neighbor has no curve there and extends >=0.75px underneath (apron), so there exist no coincident independent fits to disagree, and renderer rounding cannot expose background. The white background rect is replaced by an inferred bottom shape. STAIRCASES: the global fallback is dismantled into a per-shape candidate ladder (template -> merged -> free-form -> region-native); a staircase can only ever appear for one shape after four attempts, and the text/tiny gates that currently CAUSE staircases are replaced by coverage-matching gates. WOBBLE: data terms exist only on owned arcs with the directional-interval DP; amodal segments are pure-fairness clothoids/biarcs that cannot wobble by construction; template shapes have no sampled outline at all. CURVATURE STEPS: amodal bridges are G1-always/G2-when-stable Euler-spiral segments; clothoid endpoint drift on owned arcs is absorbed at the owned/amodal boundary (the free segment takes the correction, staying in-family) instead of being smeared linearly through visible geometry. WRONG CORNERS: corners can only arise from owned-arc CNN evidence; the occluded shape is smooth through junctions by construction, and the occluder's junction vertex is pinned to the crack-graph node — the entire class of 'phantom corner where two fits meet' disappears with the shared-boundary representation. Confidence is threaded through (gap 11): Algorithm-2 removal on owned arcs receives raw CNN probabilities as a per-corner retention prior.

new_components.what: Template fits (Fitzgibbon ellipse, PCA rect, capsule, N-gon) on owned points with z-consistency containment test; merged-region hypotheses across occluders; free-form G1/G2 clothoid bridging

new_components.what: Greedy bottom-up candidate selection with description-length scoring, 4x back-to-front rasterization check (visible-region IoU, blob, owned-Hausdorff), per-shape demotion ladder

new_components.name: Owned-weighted fitting adapter
new_components.what: Per-sample weight vector through fit_segment_midpoints DP (amodal nodes get unconstrained intervals), corner CNN restricted to owned arcs, junction-pinned occluder vertices, confidence-aware Algorithm-2

risks: Z-order ambiguity in pure flat design (true abutment, no occlusion cues): mitigated by the 'abut = occlusion with zero hidden area' reduction — owner chosen by completion simplicity, apron guarantees identical seam-free emission either way; worst case is an arbitrary but harmless ownership choice

Interlocking/cyclic occlusion (Olympic rings): FAS leaves a violated edge; handled by splitting one ring at the crossings into two stacked lobes or region-native fitting for just that cluster — bounded blast radius, but genuinely fiddly to get pixel-right

Over-merging: two same-color shapes that merely touch an occluder could be wrongly fused into one; guarded by continuation-vote requirement + MDL + the rasterization verifier, but adversarial cases exist — cap of 2 bridges/shape and a synthetic false-merge probe suite needed

Amodal extensions leaking into visible area (completed shape peeking out): hard-blocked by the verifier, but frequent verifier rejections would push shapes down the ladder and cost quality — bridge curves are pre-constrained to the occluder's interior minus 0.25px to keep rejection rare
Combinatorial growth of merged-region hypotheses on busy logos: capped by same-color + continuation-vote gating; if still slow, beam width 1 (greedy) is the design default and stays interactive
Ownership flips changing corner placement between similar inputs (determinism/stability): all votes are deterministic geometry; tie-breaks by fixed region index ordering
Color re-estimation on gradient/anti-aliased regions drifting from palette coherence: 1px erosion + robust mean, and gradient shapes keep the existing gradient-stack path

Glyph router false positives sending decorative shapes to the text profile: conservative gate calibrated on the 365 annotated logos; misroute degrades gracefully (text-safe profile is stricter, not destructive)

The apron (0.75px under-extension) creates real overlaps: invisible under opaque fills, but breaks if a user re-colors a lower shape to semi-transparent — acceptable, VAI ships the same trade per forensics
staged_plan: Stage 1 — Single-owner boundaries in paper-regions mode (no completion yet): assign every interface one owner, emit the non-owner extended 0.75px underneath. GATE: zero background-through pixels in 8x-zoom rendered diff on all 11 certified logos; certified IoUs >= current (Mastercard 0.9901 etc.).

Stage 2 — Z-order inference + painter's-algorithm SVG emission (whole pipeline output is now a stack). GATE: pixel-identical or better rendering vs Stage 1 on the full harness; benchmark_stages floors hold; runtime still seconds/icon.

Stage 3 — Template amodal completion replacing the rect/ellipse pre-pass. GATE: reproduces all current occlusion-completion wins + passes 8 new synthetic occlusion probes (bar-over-circle, disc-over-rect, triple overlap) with hidden geometry within 0.5px of GT templates.

Stage 4 — Merged-region continuation completion. GATE: split-shape suite (shape cut in two by an occluder) re-emits ONE shape in >=90% of synthetic cases with zero false merges on a 50-logo negative set; IKEA oval emitted as a single ellipse.

Stage 5 — Free-form amodal bridging + per-shape regularization on complete outlines (arbitrary-angle mirror, centroid rotation, Procrustes repeats). GATE: owned-arc Hausdorff <= budget everywhere; symmetry detected on >=10 real logos where fragment-based detection failed; no regression on certified set.

Stage 6 — Glyph top layer + text-safe/coverage gate + confidence-aware removal. GATE: zero staircase fallbacks on a 100-wordmark sample (today: known IoU-gate staircase replacements); text corner event-F1 >= current 0.73 with collapse-window fix measured.

Stage 7 — Tiny-shape coverage matching. GATE: 16/24px icon suite — human-reviewed contours+corners (per review prefs) rate >=90% 'idealized correctly'; no ellipse-or-pixel-chain binary outcomes remain.
Stage 8 — Color re-estimation + inferred/transparent background. GATE: rendered MAE vs source improves on the 11 real-logo floors; alpha inputs round-trip.

Stage 9 — Head-to-head: blind A/B vs vectorizer.ai on 50 icons + 20 wordmarks + 10 tiny icons, plus seam/roundness/wobble metrics. GATE: win or tie majority in each category; hard-zero on the seam detector.
why_beats_vai: Our IKEA forensics show VAI's edge is representational (hidden-layer completion, letters on top, global optimization) — but its output is everything-as-0.01px-cubics: approximately round circles, approximately symmetric shields, approximated corners. INVERSE PAINTER adopts the winning representation and then goes where VAI structurally cannot: exact idealization with a proof of fidelity. Our circles are true circles, mirror pairs are exactly mirrored, repeated glyphs are one outline reused, corners come from a perception-calibrated detector (Hoshyari GT) rather than curvature heuristics — and every idealization is certified by deterministic re-rasterization against the source labels, so we get VAI's zero-seam, complete-shape cleanliness PLUS a level of geometric intentionality VAI's generic-cubic output never exhibits. On the three battlegrounds: tiny icons — analytic coverage matching beats any curve fitter at 16px, including theirs; text — same letters-on-top trick plus font-template snapping they don't attempt; artifacts — seams and phantom junction corners are eliminated by construction, not suppressed by smoothing. And it runs interactively on one GPU box with a deterministic, debuggable core the team can trust and extend.
